body.heading: Guess first
paragraphs: Collect a few safe, washable things with your adult: a wooden spoon, a coin, a cork, a leaf, a plastic lid, a small stone.
Before you test anything, guess. Hold each thing and say “float” or “sink.” Write your guesses on the paper.

body.heading: Test in the water
paragraphs: Your adult fills a big bowl or the sink with water. Gently place one thing at a time on the water. No dropping or splashing.
Watch what happens. Some things surprise you. A big wooden spoon can float, and a tiny coin can sink. Size is not the whole story.

body.heading: Sort your results
paragraphs: Dry your things and sort them into two groups: floaters and sinkers. Were your guesses right?
Things float when they are light for their size and push the water aside in the right way. You can just enjoy the surprise for now; the full story comes later.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: guess, test, and find out which everyday things float and which sink.

safetyNotes: An adult fills and empties the water and stays close; children should never be left alone around water, even a bowl.
